extra_misconceptions.fact: Standard office and masking tapes have aggressive adhesives that tear paper fibers upon removal, unlike low-tack drafting tape.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Masking tape or transparent office tape holds drawing paper to a drafting board just as cleanly as drafting tape.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Light construction guidelines drawn with a hard 4H or 6H lead remain barely visible on the sheet and should never be erased.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Title block guidelines should be erased after completing single-stroke Gothic lettering so the block looks clean.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Borders require a thick, dark line drawn with a softer F or HB lead, whereas guidelines need an ultra-light 4H or 6H pencil.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Border lines and construction guidelines use the same pencil lead hardness and line weight across a drawing sheet.

extra_misconceptions.fact: An ANSI B-size sheet measures 11 by 17 inches, which doubles only the short 8.5-inch side of an 8.5 by 11-inch A-size sheet.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Standard ANSI B-size architectural and engineering sheets measure exactly twice the width and length of an A-size sheet.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to your orthographic view spacing if you select a sheet size before sketching the part dimensions and layout?
Which lead grade produces crisp, dense border lines without smudging across the paper when your triangle slides over them?
Where should a drafter anchor the corners of the vellum sheet with drafting tape to keep the T-square aligned to the edge?
What measurement confirms that your light guideline spacing matches the standard fraction height for title block lettering?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Drawing with a pencil along a scale wears down the calibrated markings and warps the edge; only triangles and T-squares guide lines.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Triangular architect's and engineer's scales serve as straightedges for drawing pencil lines along a T-square.

extra_misconceptions.fact: A visible gap of about one-sixteenth of an inch must separate the object corner from the start of the extension line.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Extension lines must touch the corners of the visible object lines so the machinist knows where the measurement starts.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Double dimensioning violates ASME standards and causes manufacturing conflicts when tolerances accumulate or one view changes.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Repeating the same overall length dimension on both the front and top orthographic views makes a drawing easier to read.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Center lines must extend uniformly past the perimeter of the circular feature by about one-eighth to one-quarter of an inch.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Center lines terminate right at the outer circle edge of a drilled hole in an orthographic mechanical view.

extra_socratic_questions: Under what condition does a hidden line take precedence over a center line when two features align in an orthographic view?
Why is it dangerous to scale distances directly off a printed manual drawing with a ruler on the manufacturing shop floor?
Which physical indicator on a triangular architect's scale prevents you from reading the wrong ratio from the opposite end?
Where should a Scout position extension lines relative to the object outline so a machinist never confuses them with part edges?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Model space geometry is always drawn at full 1:1 real-world size, and scaling occurs only within the paper space layout viewport.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Large architectural floor plans should be drawn scaled down inside CAD model space so they fit inside the screen border.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Visual placement leaves microscopic gaps or overlaps that break CNC toolpaths; always engage endpoint or intersection object snaps.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Zooming in closely on the monitor and clicking by eye connects two CAD line endpoints accurately enough for CNC machining.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Separate named layers with ByLayer linetype and lineweight properties allow teams to toggle visibility and plot standards cleanly.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Putting visible edges, hidden lines, and dimensions on Layer 0 with manual color overrides simplifies CAD file management.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Manual text overrides break associative dimensioning and leave the underlying 3D model or 2D geometry at the wrong physical size.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Overwriting the dimension text string manually is the best way to fix a measurement error on a CAD shop drawing.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to your dimension values if you draw geometry at half size in model space instead of true 1:1 full scale?
Which CAD object snap setting guarantees that a tangent arc connects cleanly to a circle without leaving an open gap?
Under what condition does freezing a CAD layer affect system regeneration differently than turning that layer off?
What measurement confirms that your paper space viewport scale matches the ratio recorded inside the CAD title block?

extra_misconceptions.fact: The revision block is a permanent chronological log that must retain earlier entries so engineers can track every design change.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Previous rows in the drawing revision table should be deleted whenever a new revision letter is released to manufacturing.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Redline refers to the reviewer's red ink or digital markups on a check print requesting additions, deletions, or dimension fixes.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Redline markups on a check print mean that only red-colored lines exist on the final production engineering drawing.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Every added or removed component on an assembly view requires an immediate quantity or item row update in the Bill of Materials.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Adding an extra mounting bracket to a mechanical assembly drawing leaves the Bill of Materials table unchanged.

extra_misconceptions.fact: A stainless steel erasing shield isolates the target line and prevents friction from tearing thin vellum or smudging nearby views.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Erasing a manual pencil revision works best by scrubbing rapidly without a backing shield across the vellum surface.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to part traceability in a machine shop if you fix a redlined dimension without incrementing the revision letter?
Where should a Scout place the revision triangle callout and revision table on an engineering drawing sheet?
Which physical tool allows you to erase a single redlined feature on a manual pencil drawing without wiping out adjacent lines?
Why is it dangerous to discard the counselor's redlined markup before verifying every change against the updated BOM table?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Two-dimensional CAD stores independent lines and arcs, while parametric modelers build 3D solids driven by feature history trees.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Two-dimensional drafting programs and three-dimensional parametric solid modelers store part geometry in the exact same way.

extra_misconceptions.fact: CAD software automates line generation, but the drafter still chooses view placement, datum selection, and ASME tolerance callouts.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Using CAD software eliminates the need for a drafter to know orthographic projection rules or standard dimensioning practices.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Manual drafting requires erasing and redrawing every affected projection view by hand whenever a part's length or profile changes.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Stretching a feature during a manual paper revision automatically updates the adjoining side view and section view dimensions.

extra_misconceptions.fact: A standard 2D PDF captures only static vector print lines; sharing editable solid geometry requires native files or STEP exports.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Exporting a 3D CAD model to a flat PDF file preserves the parametric feature tree for another engineer to edit later.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to associative dimensions and orthogonal views in parametric CAD when you modify a single feature on the part?
Under what condition does a quick manual pencil sketch on grid paper beat launching a 3D parametric CAD workstation?
Which workflow difference made executing the requirement 4 redline faster in your CAD file than on your manual vellum sheet?
What file format distinction separates a native parametric CAD assembly from a neutral exchange file like STEP or DXF?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Single-stroke means the width of each stem or curve equals the thickness of one pencil stroke, though letters use multiple strokes.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Single-stroke Gothic lettering means writing each alphabet character without ever lifting the pencil tip off the drawing paper.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Engineering drawings use all-uppercase single-stroke Gothic characters so microfilm or half-size prints stay clear and unambiguous.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Mixing lowercase and uppercase cursive handwriting is acceptable on engineering blueprints as long as the writer is neat.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Requirement 6 prohibits templates and lettering guides for forming characters; only parallel pencil guidelines may assist your hand.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Plastic lettering stencils and Ames lettering guides are permitted for writing the body text in requirement 6.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Slowly rotating the pencil between strokes wears the graphite tip evenly so letter stems keep a uniform line width across the page.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Rotating a conical mechanical pencil lead never matters during long paragraphs of hand lettering on vellum.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to the legibility of a reduced-scale blueprint if you add decorative serifs or curls to your hand lettering?
Which stroke sequence keeps the crossbar of a capital letter A or H balanced in single-stroke Gothic hand lettering?
Where should a drafter rest a protective scrap sheet under the hand while lettering a long paragraph from top to bottom?
Under what condition does uneven spacing between words make technical notes harder to read than slight slant variations?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Professional workplaces use Product Data Management vaults to enforce check-in locks, revision history, and release sign-off.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Commercial engineering firms store production CAD models on individual desktop hard drives without centralized version control.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Many fabrication shops and construction sites still plot large-format check prints for floor inspections and redline markups.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Modern CAD models never leave the computer screen because factories and construction crews have stopped using paper prints.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Electronics drafters use EDA schematic and PCB trace routing software, whereas civil drafters use GIS and corridor terrain tools.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Electronic printed circuit board drafters use the exact same civil terrain modeling tools as highway survey drafters.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Industrial facilities enforce strict non-disclosure and export-control rules that forbid photographing proprietary drawings.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Visitors touring a manufacturing plant may freely take smartphone photos of unreleased blueprints on drafting tables.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to version control in an engineering office when two drafters edit local copies of a drawing without a PDM vault?
Which physical output device in a commercial design firm prints full-size 24 by 36-inch architectural D-size check plots?
Under what condition does an architectural or manufacturing workplace still rely on hand sketching alongside CAD workstations?
Why is it dangerous to photograph proprietary drawings or monitor screens during a tour of an engineering workplace?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Many employers hire drafters with a two-year associate degree or technical diploma from an accredited community college program.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Every entry-level CAD technician job requires a four-year university bachelor's degree in mechanical or civil engineering.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Only a licensed Architect or Professional Engineer holds the legal authority to seal construction drawings for public safety.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A certified architectural drafter can legally stamp and seal structural building plans for municipal permit approval.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Experienced drafters frequently advance into senior CAD designer, BIM coordinator, checker, or engineering project manager roles.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Career growth in drafting stops at entry-level trace work with no path toward design leadership or project management.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Vendor exams test specific software tools like AutoCAD or SolidWorks, while ADDA exams test broad ASME and ANSI drafting standards.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Vendor-specific CAD certificates and ADDA Certified Drafter credentials measure the exact same software keystroke skills.

extra_socratic_questions: What distinguishes the legal stamp authority of a licensed Professional Engineer from the role of a senior CAD drafter?
Which industry certification demonstrates entry-level proficiency in American Design Drafting Association or CAD standards?
What educational pathway allows a high school graduate to enter mechanical or civil drafting in two years with low debt?
